description: ENVI-met is microclimate software for designing cities without urban heat islands, which its maker says is backed by more than 4,000 research citations. It simulates heat stress as people experience it from a physical model of the whole environment, not simplified estimates. Modules cover three-dimensional sun, shadow and reflection analysis, dispersion, transformation and deposition of reactive and non-reactive pollutants with custom vehicle fleet emissions, high-resolution facade and wall temperatures with estimates of building energy use, green and blue technologies, wind flow, outdoor thermal comfort, vegetation and humidity. Coverage: site to neighbourhood scale anywhere; case studies include Kolkata, Lagos, Parma, Lima, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Milan and Bolzano. Access: purchased licences, with business subscriptions, university licences for up to 50 devices per department, and one-year student licences without parallel computing. Licence: commercial. Caveats: licences are subscriptions or fixed term, and student licences exclude parallel computing. Simulation uses: testing greening, shading and materials for pedestrian heat stress and building surface temperatures. Related records: the ENVI-met Milan and Pescara microclimate data.
